external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A person who writes changes, pushes branches, and can log in to the build runner to start a rebuild.
external_entities.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
external_entities.notes: The text does not state the developers' trust-zone placement or authentication details.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
external_entities.notes: The text does not state the registry's authentication or protocol.

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: Picks up merges, fetches source, resolves the dependency lockfile, produces container images, pushes images to the image registry, calls the deploy controller, and can be used to start a manual rebuild.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on downloads from the public package registry.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: Maintains the current release image SHA for the estate and answers store-server release queries.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.
processes.notes: The controller is called with a shared build token. The text does not state what store servers present to it.

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store's back office that checks the current release, pulls an image when needed, and restarts the container.
processes.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
processes.notes: There are about 1,200 store-server instances. The text does not state what a store server presents to the registry or controller.

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Software running as a container on each store server.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container
processes.notes: The text does not describe the till software's data or interfaces.

data_stores.name: self-hosted git server
data_stores.description: The self-hosted Git server where developers push branches and from which the build runner fetches source.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry where the build runner stores finished container images, tagged with commit SHAs, and from which store servers pull images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_stores.notes: The registry is in the build environment, is reachable from the store estate over the WAN, allows the pull, and nobody has documented whether it encrypts what it stores.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes a branch to the self-hosted Git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_flows.notes: The text does not state the protocol, authentication, or transport encryption.

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches source from the self-hosted Git server after a merge.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches out to the public package registry while resolving the dependency lockfile.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes a finished container image to the image registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit SHA. The text does not state the protocol, authentication, or transport encryption.
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: set current release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: image SHA and shared build token

data_flows.name: check current release
data_flows.description: Each store server asks the deploy controller what the current release is.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: The text does not state what a store server presents to the controller.

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current image from the image registry when its running image differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it pulls that image from the registry and restarts the container
data_flows.notes: The registry allows the pull, but the text does not state what a store server presents to it.

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: This path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.
data_flows.data_description: login credentials and rebuild request for main

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the self-hosted Git server and deploy controller run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the self-hosted git server, which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate build environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The estate of approximately 1,200 stores containing the store servers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: retail WAN
trust_boundaries.description: The WAN carrying traffic between the stores and the corporate network.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Traffic between the stores and the corporate network goes over the retail WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet reached for dependency resolution.
